paper.title: What Memory Do GUI Agents Really Need? From Passive Records to Active Task-Driving States
paper.central_claim: GUI-agent memory should be an agent-maintained, structured, item-status-tracking execution state (ATMem) rather than a passive record; trained by verified SFT and interventional memory-ON/OFF online RL (STR-GRPO), ATMem-UI reaches 76.6% on AndroidWorld with 8B, 23.3% on unseen-environment MobileWorld, and does best among end-to-end agents on the new DataScope benchmark.

evidence.quote: Passive records preserve past snippets but do not provide stable execution-state awareness, leading to missed, repeated, or over-scoped operations.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap.

evidence.quote: we argue that GUI-agent memory should be an active task-driving state rather than an archive of past observations
evidence.support_explanation: Central design claim.

evidence.quote: is inserted into the system prompt as the current task-driving memory
evidence.support_explanation: ATMem is carried in the prompt each step; history remains available.

evidence.quote: However, SFT only imitates memory patterns observed in successful rollouts and does not estimate whether ATMem contributes to the current policy’s execution.

evidence.quote: During paired rollouts, we intervene on the explicit ATMem channel by enabling or masking memory access while keeping the task initialization unchanged.
evidence.support_explanation: Intervention mechanism: ON/OFF within a group.

signatures.object: Agent-written structured execution state (ATMem) carried in the system prompt: workflow fields (phase, remaining/completed files, constraints) and schema-level item entries with status.
signatures.information: Instruction, current screenshot, history, previous memory block; the agent updates memory each turn; teacher (LLM planner + UIIns) generates SFT memory states.
signatures.operation: SFT on 21,713 verifier-gated steps from 1.1K executable instances, then online RL.
signatures.output: Memory block, reasoning trace, executable GUI action per step.
signatures.conditions: Data-dependent multi-item cross-app workflows; memory empty when not needed.
signatures.feedback: Terminal-state verifier V in {0,1} and a memory-active cost.
signatures.selection_rule: SFT: keep trajectories whose terminal state passes the verifier. RL: group-normalised advantage over a balanced ON/OFF mixture.
signatures.persistence: Memory persists within the episode only; training result persists in policy weights.
signatures.later_use: Next-step prompt; evaluation on AndroidWorld, MobileWorld, DataScope.
signatures.failure_boundary: Stuck loops, wrong termination and step caps remain; DataScope SR stays at 1-2 of 32.

signatures.information: Same task, same initial state; half the rollouts mask the memory channel.
signatures.operation: Reward R = V(terminal) - alpha*z*rho (fraction of memory-active steps); advantage over the pooled group; ATMem tokens masked from loss in OFF rollouts.
signatures.conditions: Memory-OFF rollouts see a state the SFT policy was not trained on (OFF is out-of-distribution for imitation).
signatures.failure_boundary: alpha not reported; effect measured in single runs.

signatures.object: DataScope benchmark: 32 templates x 3 difficulty levels, target and same-schema distractor counts scaled.
signatures.information: Initializer writes targets/distractors into app storage; verifiers read terminal app state; metrics SR, App-Prog, Scope-F1.
signatures.operation: Template instantiation by LLM, verifier synthesis, calibration against controlled terminal-state variants.
signatures.selection_rule: verifier retained only if all calibration cases match
signatures.claimed_effect: Exposes stuck loops (40.9% of MAI-UI failures).

gap.author_gap: Passive records of past observations do not give stable execution-state awareness for long-horizon, multi-item, cross-app GUI workflows, causing missed, repeated or over-scoped operations.
gap.checked_gap: Supported by failure analysis of a baseline (stuck loops 40.9%) and an illustrative flat-note failure, and by the 83% data-operation share in AndroidWorld; but the quantitative flat-memory comparison sits in a figure, and the DataScope benchmark is built by the same authors around the claimed bottleneck.
lineage: Mobile-Agent-E / v2 notes memory, AgentProg program-based context, UI-Mem, MemGUI-Bench, AndroTMem and others (cited in Related Work, not pinned)
MAI-UI online RL infrastructure (pinned; their stated basis for the RL stack)
AWM/SkillWeaver-type cross-episode memory (pinned) are experience-oriented, a different axis
gap.lineage_note: Related Work separates experience-oriented from execution-oriented memory; closest execution-oriented neighbours are not available locally. MAI-UI (pinned) gives the 8B baseline at 70.7 and a 235B model at 76.7.
gap.closest_adjacent: Recording-centric note memory (Mobile-Agent-E) compared qualitatively; AgentProg for belief-state tracking.
gap.residue: Wrong termination and step-cap failures; DataScope floor effects.
gap.method_response: Make the memory itself a structured per-item status board and train when to use it.
gap.remaining_gap: Isolating the structure effect from in-environment SFT; quantitative comparison with other execution-oriented memories.
unresolved: Is the +23.1 SFT gain due to ATMem or in-environment data?

claims.text: ATMem-UI-8B reaches 76.6% on AndroidWorld, beating UI-TARS-2-230B (73.3) and 8B peers (MAI-UI 70.7, GUI-Owl-1.5-Thinking 71.6).
claims.setting: Qwen3-VL-8B + SFT on 21.7K steps + STR-GRPO; AndroidWorld 116 tasks
claims.baseline_control: Published numbers for other agents; own ablation chain Baseline 47.6 -> SFT 70.7 -> GRPO 74.8 -> STR-GRPO 76.6
claims.selection_vs_test: 20-app virtual training platform built in AndroidWorld style; overlap not analysed
claims.result_denominator: run count unstated; rates not multiples of 1/116
claims.counterevidence: MAI-UI-235B scores 76.7 in a pinned source and is not in the table; ATMem-free SFT arm absent.
claims.allowed_conclusion: In the authors setting the full pipeline outperforms listed 8B and 230B baselines on AndroidWorld; the memory structure contribution itself is not isolated.

claims.text: Structured memory generalises to unseen MobileWorld environments (23.3 vs 16.1 for GELab-Zero 4B).
claims.selection_vs_test: author statement that environments are unseen
claims.counterevidence: No app-overlap analysis; MobileWorld contains different task types (author text) which could favour the training.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Consistent ordering vs listed baselines on a second online benchmark; unseen-ness not verified by us.

claims.text: STR-GRPO yields selective memory use and higher SR than GRPO.
claims.counterevidence: Alpha and learning rate unstated; one run
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directional: Mem% down 14 points with SR up 1.8-2.6 points.

claims.text: DataScope exposes stuck loops and ATMem-UI is best among end-to-end agents at every level.
claims.counterevidence: GPT-5.2+UIIns is far higher on V1/V2 progress and scope.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directional only; success counts too small for ranking.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: An 8B Qwen3-VL policy trained with verified teacher SFT on AndroidWorld-style tasks and interventional RL scores 76.6% on AndroidWorld and 23.3% on MobileWorld in the authors runs and cuts memory use by about 16-20 points relative to SFT; the claim that structured active memory (rather than environment-matched training) causes the gains is not isolated, and DataScope shows floor effects.
unresolved: Flat-memory vs ATMem under equal training
assessment.retention: Training-time: before (SFT policy) -> candidates (ON/OFF rollouts) -> selection (verifier outcome minus memory cost, group-normalised) -> persisted in policy weights -> later AndroidWorld/MobileWorld/DataScope tasks -> measured Table 4 gain (+1.8/+2.6 over GRPO). The memory itself is not retained across tasks.

G.reason: Specific bottleneck (state tracking over multi-item cross-app workflows) with failure evidence (stuck loops 40.9%, flat-note case) and an explicit experience vs execution memory lineage; not 4 because the quantitative flat-memory comparison is figure-only, execution-oriented neighbours are not compared in tables, and the benchmark confirming the gap is self-built.

M.reason: Item-status memory schema, harvest/execute phases and the ON/OFF interventional reward form a coherent, falsifiable account (stuck loops should fall; Mem% should shrink without SR loss), with predictions checked on Mem% and failure types; the OFF condition being out-of-distribution for an imitation policy weakens the utility estimate.

X.reason: Memory structure, update loop, SFT construction, RL objective and infrastructure are specified; deductions for the two prompt boxes absent, alpha and learning rate missing, evaluation step cap unknown and no template-overlap statement.

E.measurement.reason: Executable AndroidWorld/MobileWorld checkers plus DataScope verifiers calibrated on GPT-5.2-perturbed terminal states with a retain-or-correct gate give credible success measurement; deductions for no legal-alternative pool, non-integer AndroidWorld rates and floor-level DataScope SR.

E.causality.reason: Stage chain with STR-GRPO vs GRPO and Mem%, and a within-training ON/OFF intervention, support the RL part; the central structure claim lacks an ATMem-free SFT arm and a trained flat-memory arm, the teacher is a stronger proprietary planner, and the flat-memory comparison is a single qualitative case.

E.holdout.reason: MobileWorld offers a second online benchmark described as unseen, and DataScope is new; but AndroidWorld shares apps with the training platform, no template or app overlap analysis is given, and DataScope is built by the same pipeline.

E.statistics.reason: No runs or intervals; AndroidWorld rates are not integer fractions of 116; DataScope SRs differ by one task of 32; failure percentages lack denominators.

E.cost.reason: Training cost is stated (128 H20 GPUs, about 3 days RL, 2 h SFT, 200 containers) and memory-use fraction is reported, but no inference tokens/latency/steps for carrying memory every step, and no compute-matched baseline.
